issues.legal_issue: A special community custom that gives daughters a share in property under a form of maternal-line partition is not established merely by earlier decisions that did not determine the custom on evidence.
material_facts: The claimant sought a share in her father's property under a special form of a community custom that entitled daughters to share according to the number of wives.
The claimant relied on earlier decisions rather than on evidence in the case to establish that special custom.
Only one cited decision directly mentioned the special custom; that mention was a passing observation, was not based on discussion of evidence, and was unnecessary to the decision in that case.
A later local court decision recognizing the special custom relied on that passing observation rather than evidence adduced in that case.
The general form of the community custom was recognized in other decisions, but the special form claimed was not established by evidence in the cited decisions.
issues.conclusion: The special custom giving daughters a share was not established, so the claimant could not succeed on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: A custom contrary to ordinary Hindu law must ordinarily be alleged and proved. Under section 57(1) of the Evidence Act, proof may become unnecessary when a custom has been recognized and affirmed in a series of decisions, each based on evidence in the particular case, so that it becomes incorporated into the general law. Earlier decisions that do not establish the custom on evidence, or contain only an unnecessary passing observation about it, do not satisfy that standard. The Court relied on Rama Rao v. Rajah of Pittapur, Premraj v. Chand Kunwar, and Ujagar Singh v. Mst. Jeo.

rule.if: special_custom_inheritance_claim and prior_decisions_relied_on and not prior_decisions_established_custom_on_evidence and not independent_evidence_established_custom

predicates.special_custom_inheritance_claim: A claimant seeks an inheritance share under a special community custom that extends the usual form of partition to daughters.
predicates.prior_decisions_relied_on: The claimant relies on earlier court decisions to establish the special custom.
predicates.prior_decisions_established_custom_on_ev: The earlier decisions recognized the special custom on the basis of evidence adduced in those cases.
predicates.independent_evidence_established_custom: Evidence in the present case independently establishes the special custom.

issues.definition: When an inheritance claim under a special custom rests on earlier decisions that did not establish the custom through evidence, and no independent evidence establishes it, the special custom is not established.
